# Lorna Vane

## Overview

- **Age:** Twenty-eight years old  <sub>[v4 c13 P15](../source/v04-c13.md#nw-v04-c13-p0015)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v4 c10 P10](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0010), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- **Origin:** Seven Gulls  <sub>[v4 c11 P4](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0004), [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015)</sub>
- **Role:** Former schoolteacher and landlady  <sub>[v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c11 P35](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0035), [v4 c23 P28](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0028)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Lorna  <sub>[v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029)</sub>

## Appearance

Lorna is a bright, strikingly lovely woman with ocean-blue eyes and a figure of fine contour and marble-like arms. She possesses hair that glisten and shimmers like liquid gold, falling clear to her feet in length. She has work-hardened brown hands from years of labor and frequently wears a splash or belt of red on her simple attire.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c12 P5](../source/v04-c12.md#nw-v04-c12-p0005), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 c17 P10](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0010), [v4 c21 P17](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0017), [v4 c23 P24](../source/v04-c23.md#nw-v04-c23-p0024), [v4 c26 P18](../source/v04-c26.md#nw-v04-c26-p0018), [v4 c38 P1](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0001), [v4 c38 P10](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0010)_

## Personality

Lorna possesses a deep, strong character shaped by grief and governed by a strict sense of duty. Though she can be distant, reserved, and subject to stern or gloomy moods, she blossoms into an engaging, humorous, and sharp-witted companion among close friends. She is a graceful dancer with a passionate, wild love of freedom and nature. In her heart she harbors a loyal, sympathetic spirit and a deep devotion to her ideals.

_Sources: [v4 c11 P15](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0015), [v4 c11 P22](../source/v04-c11.md#nw-v04-c11-p0022), [v4 c16 P5](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0005), [v4 c16 P11](../source/v04-c16.md#nw-v04-c16-p0011), [v4 c17 P10](../source/v04-c17.md#nw-v04-c17-p0010), [v4 c25 P15](../source/v04-c25.md#nw-v04-c25-p0015), [v4 c30 P27](../source/v04-c30.md#nw-v04-c30-p0027), [v4 c40 P50](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0050)_

## History

Lorna grew up in Seven Gulls as the intelligent and cheerful daughter of Frank Ainslie and Rose Kerr. Tragedies struck her youth when she witnessed her younger brother Julian's fatal accident at age twelve, followed two years later by discovering her father's suicide. Funded by her grandmother's legacy, she completed two years of study in one at Regent's Academy and became a beloved teacher at the Glen school. To save her mother from financial ruin, she yielded to pressure and married Rufus Vane, though she did not love him. After her husband vanished and was later returned brain-damaged like a child, Lorna spent eleven years faithfully caring for him in solitude while leasing her farm to survive.

Following the arrival of Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow, Lorna initially kept her distance out of envy for Nell's happiness, but she gradually overcame her reticence and formed a deep, devoted friendship with Nell. When guest Adrian Treleaven stayed in the area, Lorna found joy in his companionship and helped inspire his writing. Though bound by her unyielding sense of duty when faced with her husband's potential medical treatment, subsequent events freed her from her past. Moving into the house of dreams to assist Nell, Lorna accepted Adrian's love, with their wedding planned for Christmas.

## Quotes

> You must address me as Lorna if we are to be friends  <sub>[v4 c10 P29](../source/v04-c10.md#nw-v04-c10-p0029)</sub>

> I ENVY Nell, and even if she had died, I’d still envy her! For one beautiful day, she was a mother. For THAT, I’d give my life gladly!  <sub>[v4 c19 P28](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0028)</sub>

> My hatred for you stemmed from my ENVY toward you—oh, at intervals I was utterly consumed with envy of you. You possessed a sweet tiny house—plus affection—plus joy—plus cheerful visions—all the things I desired—yet lacked entirely—and could not possibly attain.  <sub>[v4 c21 P11](../source/v04-c21.md#nw-v04-c21-p0011)</sub>

> I will miss him greatly.  <sub>[v4 c28 P26](../source/v04-c28.md#nw-v04-c28-p0026)</sub>

> Oh, Nell, Nell, you have proved to be such an incredible friend—'a good, sweet woman—true and faithful and to be depended on’—as Captain Saul described you.  <sub>[v4 c38 P31](../source/v04-c38.md#nw-v04-c38-p0031)</sub>
